rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb when something causes mental distress or persistently affects someone physically.

example.english: This matter continues to trouble me.
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 zung6 kwan3 jiu2 zyu6 ngo5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a concrete problem, including a health or mechanical problem.
Use this for bothering or inconveniencing someone, especially in polite requests such as 唔好麻煩你.

example.english: Please don't trouble yourself; I can carry it myself.
example.traditional: 唔好麻煩你喇，我自己攞得喇。
example.jyutping: m4 hou2 maa4 faan4 nei5 laa3 ngo5 zi6 gei2 lo2 dak1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for being in a difficult situation or for extra inconvenience; in a legal context it can mean being in trouble with the authorities without naming the legal issue.

example.english: We’re in trouble this time—the police arrested us.
example.traditional: 我哋今次麻煩喇，俾警察拉咗。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 ci3 maa4 faan4 laa3 bei2 ging2 caat3 laai1 zo2

rows.note: Use this specifically for difficulty in carrying out an action or task.

example.english: I have trouble moving this table by myself.
example.traditional: 我一個人搬呢張枱有困難。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 go3 jan4 bun1 ni1 zoeng1 toi2 jau5 kwan3 naan4

rows.note: Use this for mental distress, worry, or a troubled state of mind rather than an external problem.

example.english: Job hunting has been causing me a lot of trouble lately.
example.traditional: 最近搵工搞到我好煩惱。
example.jyutping: zeoi3 gan6 wan2 gung1 gaau2 dou2 ngo5 hou2 faan4 nou5
